links.reason: Line 3 of 188 (முக்கண் சினம் திகழ் விடையினானும் செல்வியும் சேர்ந்தது ஒத்தே) only compares the pair to the god and goddess; it makes no claim about the union, so there is nothing for 208's பெரும் பழி to contradict. The counsellor cites Siva's half-body as blame in his own argument; he does not turn the narrator's simile, so 'tension' is a shared figure.

Both use the sea for the host, but 873 has bells and conches roaring (மால்கடல் எழுந்தன) while 950 says the sea of troops looks like the milk-sea (பாற்கடல்). The shift from noise to heavenly calm is read in, not stated; the link is a shared simile.

1174 has the king declare he is faultless and then enter the council hall (மந்திர சாலை சேர்ந்தான்); he does consult. Kural 568 faults a king who does not think matters through with his circle. The note makes the epic the reverse of the rule and calls the thunder a rage that precedes counsel, which the verse does not show.
links.text_issue: Spy's first-person line 4; sense not tied to anger.

links.reason: Both verses have Vijayai on the peacock machine, but வினைமயில் in 2614 line 3 is flagged uncertain and may mean the machine of the deed or simply the working machine. Reading it as fate's instrument is the marker's guess, and the teaches rests on it.

Paripadal 5 lines 15-17 say the velan's veri exists and is neither true nor false (வாயும் அல்ல, பொய்யும் அல்ல) because the world has its bound in the god; Akananuru 242 line 10 calls the velan அறியா. The Paripadal limits the akam mockery without rejecting it, as the note says.

Line 2 has the king ordering the merchants' wealth and the buffalo (மயிடம்) seized, not a horse as the note says. The verse does not condemn or say a report was unexamined, so the teaches about an unexamined report is not in the Tamil; it illustrates Kural 551 without adding to it.

401 shows Sunandai and her husband welcoming and keeping the cured ascetic; nothing in the Tamil says he came hungry, was of hidden worth, or is a Vidyadhara king. The measure by the guest's worth in Kural 87 (துணைத்துணை வேள்விப் பயன்) is not tested by what the verse says.

2985 line 4 calls the fruit of good deeds a poison (நல்வினை விளையுள் என்னும் நஞ்சு) and 2846 line 3 makes release freedom from deeds (வினை விடுதல்); the later verse states for good deeds what the sermon leaves general. Line 2 of 2985 is obscure but line 3-4 carry the claim.

Civakan's line 3 says the great bear the wrongs of the small (பெரியவர் ... பொறுப்பர்), the same idea as Naladiyar 77, but no run of words is shared and the verse itself says nothing of his denying fault. The flattery-that-obliges reading comes from the marker's nuance, not from the Tamil.

1129 follows 1128 directly in the song-and-reaction order; sequence is not a link. The song warns the kurava tree that young men will pluck it (இளையராற் ... பறிப்புண்டி), not the groom, and the smile is only said to come after hearing, not to answer.

Udayana 4 speaks of deeds shed in order (வரிசையின் உதிர்ப்பை) and Naga 4 of deeds shed in a moment (கணத்தினில் உதிர்ப்பை); that is a difference, not a development. Both verses are hard to parse and the proem formula may be shared, so 'adds order and ripening' overreads.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain; first two lines of each hard to parse.

links.reason: 215 shows Yugi and Salankayan talking of dharma texts and the king rejoicing in Yugi; nothing says a quarrel ends or that Salankayan 'ran the trap'. 41 only has him showing the artificial elephant. The link depends on a plot the verses do not state.

242 line 3-4 says kings grasp subtle matters only through treatises; Kural 637 says act by knowing how the world goes after knowing the method. These speak of understanding and of acting; the verse does not say books alone suffice, so they do not conflict.

2619 is a call to do penance before youth passes, spoken to listeners; 2848 has the king bathing in the sage's dharma. Nothing in the Tamil says the sermon makes the king act on Vijayai's exhortation; this is two verses in one chapter.

1763 only describes the drum, smeared with sandal and struck (பலிபெறு முரசம் ... அதிர்ந்தறைந்தவே); it gives no hint of death or impermanence. The shadow the note sees comes from Naladiyar 23's மணப்பறை/பிணப்பறை, which the epic verse does not touch.

Innaa 36 line 1 counts as painful the poor man's wish to be liberal; Kural 218 praises those who do not falter in ஒப்புரவு without means. The pain of unfulfilled giving is real, but the Innaa man is not the Kural's giver, so qualifies is thin.

2551 echoes 465 (the mother's penance behind the son), as the note says. But nothing in the Tamil makes it a verdict on his rule, and whether the woman changes from bearer to raiser is unsettled by the words (the marker says so); the teaches is imposed.

Mani 26 line 2-4 names both Kannaki and Kovalan in the image; Sil 28:222-234 never says the image is of Kannaki alone, and the Mani lines do not say this is Senguttuvan's shrine. The 'alone versus family' contrast and the household reshaping are not in the cited lines.

Neelakesi 86 line 3 says penance removes dark karma; Soolamani 2115 draws a sword of meditation (தியானம் என்னும் கொற்றவாள்) against an enemy's unrestraint, and the verse does not mention karma. 'Both say karma is removed by effort' is true only if the marker's gloss of the sword is accepted.

Yasodhara 70's verbs have the hearing itself check and shed karma (ஊற்றுச் செறித்து உதிர்ப்பை ஆக்கும்); it is not the hearer's own effort, so 'in one the hearer does the work' misreads it. Tirumanthiram 1527 has grace as guru and the end of தன்செயல். The clash is drawn from doctrine, not from these words.

Neelakesi 499 argues that nothing is known except through its qualities (குணமுகத்தால் அன்றி), against the Buddha; Kural 355's எப்பொருள் எத்தன்மைத்தாயினும் ... மெய்ப்பொருள் காண்பது is about seeing the true thing. No words are shared except எப்பொருளும், and 'not stripping them away' is not in the Kural.

55 has kings under his feet, sages under his crown and the world cool under the umbrella; 69 has the earth asleep under it while the king bathes in the queens. Both describe the same king in the same chapter; protection-to-pleasure is the note's reading of the order.

2794 line 3-4 has the teacher say householders are worn down bearing the yoke (நுகம் பூண்டார்); Kural 46 asks what a virtuous householder gains by going outside. This is a defensible clash on whether the household is the way, and gains are specific. The verse is flagged uncertain.

319 has Vijayai say she did no good deeds (நல்வினை செய்து இலாதேன்); 343 is a dawn simile about evil deeds leaving when old good deeds come forward (தொல்லை நல்வினை முற்பட). The narrator does not name her merit or overrule her; the simile is about dawn.

773 says princes do not weigh their lives when beings are in danger and have no other duty (அறம் பிறிது அதனில் உண்டோ). Kural 388 is about the ruler who does justice being counted இறை. The gains are generic: neither text needs the other.

286 only says the city is like a gods' world with endless desire (காம முடிவிலராகி ... தெய்வ உலகம்); it is a simile, not a realm without death, and the note leans on verse 278 not in the packet. Naladiyar 14's old age has no contact with it.

2056 shows her bowing with joined hands; the verse names no one she prays for and the marker takes it as before Kama. The note's 'for him in his hidden presence' is a reconstructed plot, and 899's vow needs Civakan to bow, which is not undone by her bowing to a god.

Yasodhara 153 line 3 says heaped deeds come in at death (புஞ்சிய வினைகள் தீய புகுந்தன) and send them to animal births, which fits Naladiyar 101's deeds seeking out their doer. The gains are generic and the quatrain's calf image is not in the verse.

2651 line 3-4 gives up pleasure like a rain-bubble (மழைமொக்குள்) and takes austerity; Naladiyar 53 says the best renounce. The note's husband still held by pleasure is not in the Tamil. This illustrates the quatrain rather than qualifying it.

2869 says truth reaches the towers of the upper world and the lie the great hell (பொய்யுரையும் வேண்டா); Kural 293 says the liar's own heart burns him (தன்நெஞ்சே தன்னைச் சுடும்). The two places for one cost is a true contrast, but neither verse mentions the other's side, so the gains clauses are read in.

549 line 1-2 rests the match on equal lineage and wealth, not on 'shared descent from Nami', and the name Nami is not in the verse. 427 chooses an envoy to speak of kin and business, so 549 is the envoy doing it; that is a sequence of commission and report.

83 says shame-bound women bear desire's fire most; 465 has men saying Kama's bow is bent on women's faces. Silent women against speaking men is the note's contrast; neither verse speaks of who may say it.

1517 line 1-4 is badly corrupted (நுனசீ றடிநோ வநடந் துசெலே ... பொயுரைத் தனையால் வினையே னொழியத்), so the marker's reconstructed quotation carries the note. வினையேன் and பொய்யுரைத்தனை give both the blame of herself and the lie; Kural 1154's தேறியார் asks who is at fault.

520 has foam-body (நுரைமலி பொள்ளல் யாக்கை) used in a rank argument; Naladiyar 27 has the bubble (மழை மொக்குள்) used to urge release. The inversion is real but foam and bubble are not one word, and the quatrain gains nothing from being turned to an insult.

848 line 3-4 has the sea not fetching water and the river not begging the rain; Naladiyar 103 has no one rounding the vilam fruit. Both argue from nature to a fixed lot, but the contrast of lot fixed versus flowing in is thin and 'develops' does not fit.

1351 runs through smell, taste, music, dance and touch, the five senses of Kural 1101; the Kural puts all in one woman and the epic spreads them. But the verse never contrasts itself with the couplet, and 'recognised as the Kural's scheme' is not shown by shared words.

1523 has the pearl parasol, rejoicing people and the sea-ringed world under it; it names no conquest. Kural 389 makes the world rest under a king who bears bitter words. The shared image is the parasol, and the gains are trivial.

1449 shows Asvagriva's rage and arrows (செவிசுடும் பொறுக்கலாற்றேன்); that the arrows fail and turn on him is in 1450, not in the unit. Kural 305 says anger kills its owner; this verse shows only the anger, so the cost is borrowed from the next verse.

657 has trees putting out shoots and birds forgetting themselves and falling to the ground (நிலத்திடைப் பறவை மெய்ம்மறந்து வீழ்ந்தவே); Thiruppugazh 43 has dry trees sprouting and birds coming to earth at the flute. The image is shared, but the note's 659 is not in the packet and the later hymn cannot be what the epic 'uses'.

1045 shows the maiden hiding her sickness and betrayed by pallor (பசலைமெய் புகலலுற்றதே); Kural 1183 says love gave sickness and pallor in exchange for grace and modesty. It is a fair step-by-step, but the couplet does not need a maiden before marriage, so the gains are generic.

The patikam 19 gives the two months (இரு திங்கள்) and the leaving over the mountains; 1359 gives இரண்டு திங்கள், the night departure and பொறி as his chariot. The narrative adds the heart's rising (எழுந்தது உள்ளம்) and fortune together, which the summary does not say.

829 has the Vidyadhara king resolve to give his daughter to the lion-killer; 1012 has Tivittan's mother embrace the portrait and call the match ripened tavam. The women making her a member of the family before the groom sees her is not in either verse; this is plot sequence.

495 line 4 says sulking and blaming former deeds is not understanding (உம்மைவினை நொந்து புலந்தூடல் உணர்வன்று); 510 says the good survive by the fruit of former deeds (பழவினைப் பயத்தின்). Blaming misfortune and trusting in merit are not incompatible, and the Kural is not in either verse.

1962 line 4 says desire is the one sickness with no medicine (மருந்து இல்லது); Kural 1102 says the woman is herself the cure. They contrast, but that Vimalai's despair is a stage the story resolves by marriage is outside the verse, so the gains rest on a plot the unit does not state.
